subject: HANDOFF: close-cycle prime ownership corroboration + generic-to-prime crossover
body: WORKSTREAM_ID=ws-prime-once-cycle-owner-20261001a. FINAL_MAIN_SHA=45bb0d326899c0e08415928224cfea0ff58d2d4e; unchanged from STARTING_MAIN_SHA. R&D complete; no production GitHub writes. Core finding corroborates overlapping state-rd workstream ws-state-rd-close-cycle-prime-20261001t223445z: PanelEngine-local primedContinuityCycleId is not a stable close-cycle authority, removed-engine prime callbacks survive destroy because the prime coroutine ignores captureGen, and Fold7ContinuityFrameStore accepts an older ticket after a newer capture has STARTED because publish fences only against latest PUBLISHED sequence. This work adds a distinct same-engine source path: an Accessibility continuity ticket can be admitted while privileged capture is unavailable; a later Shizuku prime can begin a newer ticket and set the local prime guard; the already-issued generic callback does not re-check that guard and current FrameStore accepts the older ticket. Direct source-faithful Kotlin reproduction: generic #1 begin -> prime #2 begin -> generic #1 publish ACCEPTED; if #2 fails, generic-accessibility remains current. Recommended reconciliation: use the overlapping workstream's richer stable owner/fallback state model, require ALL exact-cycle continuity capture admission (prime and generic fallback) to pass through one service-stable owner, make source changes explicit keep-or-supersede transitions with numbered attemptSequence, and harden FrameStore so publish requires the newest STARTED/admitted captureSequence. My pure owner prototype passed 11/11 plus 100k fixed-seed adversarial events; earlier combined model passed 10/10 plus 100k. Full handoff records confirmed source facts, rejected partial fixes, and primary validation cases. Live Agent Bus remains legacy duoopen-agentbus/v1; this work followed /messages + /artifacts and did not invent V6 lanes. Primary should merge this evidence with the overlapping state-rd 13/13 model rather than implement duplicate owners.
